saints.name: St. Anthony of Padua
saints.title: Priest and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: A Portuguese Franciscan of dazzling preaching and learning, invoked the world over for the finding of what is lost…
biography: Born Fernando Martins de Bulhões at Lisbon in 1195, Anthony entered the Augustinian canons at fifteen and was ordained priest at Coimbra. Moved by the relics of five Franciscans martyred in Morocco, he joined the Friars Minor in 1220, taking his new name from their chapel of Anthony the Great, and sailed for Morocco, only to be driven by illness and storm back to Italy.

His gifts lay hidden until an impromptu sermon at Forlì in 1222 revealed a preacher of rare power. Francis of Assisi himself entrusted to him the theological training of the friars — the order's first lector — and he taught at Bologna, Montpellier, and Toulouse, preached against heresy in France and Italy, and served as provincial of northern Italy.

He died at Arcella, on the road to Padua, on 13 June 1231, aged thirty-five, and Gregory IX canonized him at Spoleto the following May; Pius XII named him a Doctor of the Church in 1946. Because a novice who stole his annotated psalter was moved by his prayer to return it, he is invoked the world over for the finding of lost things.
saints.knownFor: His preaching and learning; patron of lost things.

canonization.canonized: 1232 by Pope Gregory IX; Doctor of the Church (1946)

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 13 June
